title: Live-Reproducible Portfolio Allocator Parity
summary: Pure Rust port of the Round 9 repaired Python allocator. Forward-only timing, weight-capped eligibility, live runtime state for trading-engine integration.

invariants_proven.forward_only_timing: Rebalance at ts only affects intervals AFTER ts. The interval [prev_ts, ts] is attributed to the previously active sleeve. Verified by allocator_switch_uses_completed_interval_only.
invariants_proven.weight_params_bind: max_high_ann_weight excludes high-ann sleeves when set to 0; min_low_dd_weight forces low-DD sleeve eligibility when > 0. Output allocation changes when these params toggle. Verified by allocator_respects_max_high_ann_and_min_low_dd_weights.
invariants_proven.no_forced_cycle_close: Existing martingale cycles are not force-closed on sleeve switch. New cycles open only for the active sleeve. Verified by live_runtime_persists_allocator_active_sleeve_until_next_rebalance.

test_counts.trading_engine_total: 195 passed across all test binaries (incl. 2 new R9 allocator tests)

public_api: AllocatorConfig { lookback_days, rebalance_days, score_function, max_high_ann_weight, min_low_dd_weight, cash_trigger_rolling_dd_pct, switch_hysteresis_score_gap, high_ann_sleeve_ids, low_dd_sleeve_ids }

live_integration_contract.description: The trading-engine main loop keeps one AllocatorState per allocator-managed portfolio. At each tick: (1) check may_open_new_cycle_for(sleeve_id, now_ms) before opening any new martingale cycle; (2) when now_ms crosses next_rebalance_ms, compute per-sleeve RollingMetrics from data <= now_ms and call rebalance(now_ms, cfg, metrics); (3) existing cycles continue running until their natural TP/SL — the allocator does not force-close them.
live_integration_contract.gap_for_full_live_deploy: trading-engine main.rs does not yet wire AllocatorState into the per-tick decision loop. The module is complete and tested; integration into the live event loop is the remaining work (does not affect backtest validity or parity proof).

parity_status.verdict: Allocator logic has live parity: the same forward-only, weight-capped, no-force-close semantics are implemented and tested in both engines. The trading-engine can host the allocator via AllocatorState; only the per-tick dispatch wiring in main.rs remains.
